title: Inside The 7 Minute Bengaluru Robbery: How Rs 7.11 Crore Vanished On A Flyover | India News - News18
text: On November 19, Dairy Circle in Bengaluru carried its usual rhythm of impatience. Cars cut lanes, bikes squeezed through gaps, buses dragged themselves up the flyover in slow bursts. Among them was a CMS cash van making its routine trip to load an ATM near South End Circle which is approximately 5 kms from diary circle. Inside the van was Rs 7.11 crore packed in sealed bags. Nothing about the vehicle stood out. It looked like it had driven this road a hundred times before. There were no clues that the next 7 minutes would unravel one of the most precise cash van robberies Bengaluru has seen. The Van That Stopped at the Wrong Moment As the van moved ahead on the flyover, an Innova eased into position in front of it. The signal came from inside the Innova, a confident wave to pull over. The men in the Innova claimed they were officials from the Reserve Bank of India. The staff inside the CMS vehicle did not argue. A city used to frequent checks and official stops often complies fast. The van slowed and halted. And the robbery began without a single shout. A Heist That Unfolded Without Noise According to the staff, the men did not waste time. There was no aggression reported. No drawn weapons. No loud instructions. They opened the rear, moved straight to the cash bags, and shifted them with a clarity that suggested planning. Then came the detail that changed the investigation. The men took the Digital Video Recorder from the van, removing the only direct evidence of the incident. In less than 7 minutes, the Innova had merged back into routine traffic, carrying Rs 7.11 crore and the DVR that should have captured every second of the operation. A Police Station Turns Into a War Room By evening, Siddapura Police Station had transformed into the centre of the investigation. Bengaluru Police Commissioner Seemant Kumar Singh arrived personally and remained there until late night. His presence signalled the seriousness of the case. Driver Binod, custodian Aftab, and gunmen Rajanna and Tammayya were questioned repeatedly. Their accounts matched. Same van. Same Innova. Same men claiming RBI authority. Same timeline that felt too quick and too clean. The Search Begins With Missing Footage With the DVR gone, the investigation turned toward digital forensics. Officers seized the phones of all CMS staff present in the van. Every call detail, deleted image, message, WhatsApp chat and location ping was checked to understand whether any information had leaked before the robbery. A tower dump of all mobile phones active around the Dairy Circle flyover during the incident was pulled. The task is massive, but it is crucial. Investigators now have to examine which devices stayed near the van, which moved away, and which unusual numbers appeared in the area at the exact time the robbery took place. Tracing the Escape Route Another set of police team focused on the roads leaving the city. One early suspicion is that the gang may have fled Bengaluru within 1 hour of the robbery. This triggered a coordinated response across major exit routes. Checkpoints at Hoskote, Hosur, Tumakuru Road, Kanakapura and Mysuru Road were alerted. Traffic police and local police jointly monitored vehicles. Every Innova that crossed toll gates in that hour was flagged. Lists of registration numbers, colours and timings are now being analysed and matched against CCTV footage. Toll gate cameras, usually scanning for routine traffic violations, have become a key part of the investigation. Officers are reviewing the footage frame by frame, looking for any Innova that stands out by timing or direction. The Question of Inside Help While the van crew has cooperated, the investigation is also probing whether internal information was shared before the robbery. Police are checking whether staff had unusual contacts or patterns in the days leading up to the incident. Reviewing staff movements from the time they left home to the time the robbery occurred is now a critical part of the probe. Even a small leak of timing or route could have helped the gang plan the stop with such precision. 7 Minutes That Created a Citywide Manhunt Multiple police teams, including the City Crime Branch, are now involved. Leads have reportedly emerged, though nothing has been officially confirmed. The Commissioner continues to oversee the investigation closely. What remains is a crime defined by silence and speed. A van stopped on a busy flyover. Men who claimed authority. Cash bags lifted without panic. A DVR removed to erase the timeline. And an Innova leaving the city before anyone realised what had happened. Rs 7.11 crore. 7 minutes. No video. A city still trying to trace the path of a gang that moved like they knew every second of the road ahead.
